claim: A PullSplit whose owner set a warehouse withdrawal incentive and left withdrawals unpaused can be drained by cycling permissionless warehouse withdraw (earning the incentive) with permissionless depositToWarehouse.
evidence: SplitsWarehouse.sol:226-250 batch withdraw pays config.incentive to caller-chosen _withdrawer and only reverts when paused; PullSplit.sol:105-107 depositToWarehouse is public/permissionless (pausable only). No code prevents the withdraw->redeposit cycle.
runtimeTrigger: Owner sets WithdrawConfig{incentive>0, paused:false} for the PullSplit address. Attacker loops: warehouse.withdraw(split, [token], [amount], attacker) then split.depositToWarehouse(token, amount), skimming incentive% each cycle.

claim: PushSplit ETH distribute sends the distributor reward with full-gas safeTransferETH, letting a malicious distributor contract reenter distribute() mid-payout and extract extra value.
evidence: PushSplit.sol:133 distributor reward sent via _distributor.safeTransferETH(distributorReward) (all gas, no stipend cap), unlike recipient sends which use trySafeTransferETH with GAS_STIPEND_NO_GRIEF.
runtimeTrigger: Attacker contract as _distributor reenters distribute() from its receive() during the reward transfer; reentrant call re-reads balances and pays a second distributor reward.

claim: PushSplit ERC20 distribute is reenterable through hook tokens (ERC777 tokensReceived), letting a malicious recipient reenter distribute() and double-pay shares.
evidence: PushSplit.sol:135-139 safeTransfer to each recipient in a loop with no reentrancy guard; an ERC777 token invokes the recipient hook during transfer, before later recipients are paid.
runtimeTrigger: Split holds an ERC777 token; malicious recipient reenters distribute() from tokensReceived; reentrant distribution pays shares again from the remaining pool.

claim: The same EOA registered at two signer indices satisfies a 2-of-n threshold with one key, defeating the m-of-n policy.
evidence: MultiSignerLib.initializeSigners and addSigner never check for duplicate signer values; isValidSignature only rejects duplicate INDICES (DuplicateSigner), not duplicate signer identities. One key signing front hash at index 0 and back hash at index 1 passes threshold 2.
runtimeTrigger: Vault configured with the same EOA at indices 0 and 1, threshold 2. Single key signs light hash (index 0) and full hash (index 1); validateUserOp returns VALID_SIGNATURE.

claim: In an ownerless SmartVault (owner == address(0)), any enabled module can upgrade the implementation via a self-call, because _checkOwner authorizes address(this) when owner is zero.
evidence: SmartVault._checkOwner returns authorized when owner==0 and caller==address(this); _authorizeUpgrade is onlyOwner; modules execute arbitrary calls as the vault via executeFromModule, so a module can call upgradeToAndCall on the vault itself.
runtimeTrigger: Ownerless vault with an enabled module; module calls executeFromModule([{target: vault, data: upgradeToAndCall(maliciousImpl, ...)}]); _checkOwner passes via the owner==0 self-call branch.

claim: Warehouse batchDeposit mints ERC6909 balances before pulling tokens, so a fee-on-transfer token leaves the warehouse insolvent (credits exceed holdings) and late withdrawers cannot claim.
evidence: SplitsWarehouse.sol:177-198 batchDeposit _mint()s each receiver inside the loop, then safeTransferFrom(sum) after; a token taking a fee delivers less than sum while full balances were credited.
runtimeTrigger: Deposit a fee-on-transfer token via batchDeposit; warehouse ERC6909 supply exceeds its token balance; final withdrawals revert on insufficient token balance.

claim: AutoEarnModule.deposit is permissionless and sweeps an account's ENTIRE asset balance into the earn vault, letting anyone force-convert a vault's liquid balance (griefing / forced fee exposure).
evidence: AutoEarnModule.sol:71-83 deposit() reads the full balance and executes approve+deposit via executeFromModule with no caller restriction; the only gate is the module being enabled on the account.
runtimeTrigger: Anyone calls deposit(victimVault) at any time; the vault's full USDC balance is swept into the ERC4626 vault, converting liquid funds to shares without the owner's action.
